note: Set A captures the 7% outfitting mass allowance (plus the 100 t transition piece) that Set B omits, while Set B restates the steel density, Young's modulus and shear modulus three times each under slightly reformatted values. Set B's extra claim on the 20–30 m clearance range is supported by the footnote, though its 'typical variation' condition is a loose paraphrase rather than text. Both sets bind the material, geometry, frequency and mass values correctly with supporting quotes.
remarks: Set B duplicates steel density (7 85E3 / 7.85E3), Young's modulus (2 00E11 / 2.00E11) and shear modulus (7 93E10 / 7.93E10) — the same table rows stated twice with different number formatting. Set B drops the 7% outfitting mass fact. Its clearance claim's condition 'typical variation' is not stated in the footnote (which only says clearances 'can vary between 20 m to 30 m' and are not specified in an official standard). Both sets omit the design constraint that the 0.170 Hz first mode lies between the 1P and 3P ranges and avoids the 0.10–0.13 Hz wave band, and the note that a stiffer tower is required for a floating/semisubmersible substructure.
